disclaimers.score_label: ATS readability score (heuristic). Not a score from any real ATS; systems differ.
disclaimers.footer: Heuristic checks, not a score from any real ATS. Evidence of use, not proficiency or authorship.
disclaimers.keyword_gap_note: This does not mean you lack the skill.

file_type.title: File Format Specification
file_type.description: Checks that the uploaded document is either a valid PDF or Microsoft Word (.docx) file.
file_type.fix: Export your document strictly as a standard PDF or .docx file.

text_extractable.title: Text Extractability
text_extractable.description: Verifies that the document contains selectable, machine-readable text above the threshold.
text_extractable.fix: Avoid saving resumes as scanned flattened images. Export directly from your word processor.

scanned_image_only.title: Scanned Document / Raster Check
scanned_image_only.description: Detects if the file is an image-only scan with no parsable text stream.
scanned_image_only.fix: Re-export your resume as a text-based PDF or DOCX file.

file_size.title: File Size Efficiency
file_size.description: Ensures document size is below 2MB for fast parsing without gateway timeouts.
file_size.fix: Compress high-resolution background assets or remove unneeded graphics.

page_count.title: Document Length / Page Count
page_count.description: Standard software engineering resumes are typically 1 to 2 pages.
page_count.fix: Trim non-essential details to keep your resume concise within 1 to 2 pages.

password_protection.title: Document Encryption & Access
password_protection.description: Ensures the document has no encryption, passwords, or permission locks.
password_protection.fix: Save an unprotected copy without passwords or permission locks.

single_column_order.title: Single-Column Reading Order
single_column_order.description: Multi-column layouts risk reading-order scrambling when parsers read horizontally across columns.
single_column_order.fix: Switch to a clean single-column layout so ATS parsers read your career timeline in sequential order.

tables_for_layout.title: Table-Based Layout Detection
tables_for_layout.description: Tables used for structural layout confuse sequential parsers and cause text fragments to merge.
tables_for_layout.fix: Replace tables with standard linear margins and bulleted lists.

header_footer_containment.title: Header & Footer Trapping
header_footer_containment.description: Key contact info (email, phone, links) placed only in header/footer zones is ignored by many parsers.
header_footer_containment.fix: Move contact details (email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub) into the top body of the document.

text_in_images.title: Text Inside Images or Icons
text_in_images.description: Contact details, skills, or titles rendered as embedded bitmap images cannot be indexed by text parsers.
text_in_images.fix: Use real text characters instead of icons or graphic images for skills and contact information.

corrupt_glyphs.title: Unusual Bullets & Special Glyphs
corrupt_glyphs.description: Non-standard bullet characters or custom fonts can extract as replacement characters (e.g., \ufffd).
corrupt_glyphs.fix: Use standard circular bullets (•) or hyphens (-) and standard system fonts.

hidden_or_white_text.title: Hidden or Micro-Font Text
hidden_or_white_text.description: Detects white-on-white text, font sizes below 2pt, or text off-canvas flagged for heuristic review.
hidden_or_white_text.fix: Remove hidden or off-canvas text. Rely on legitimate code-proven evidence instead of stuffing.

standard_headings.title: Standard Section Headings
standard_headings.description: Identifies canonical section headers (Experience, Skills, Education) using standard alias recognition.

contact_email.title: Email Address Detection
contact_email.description: Detects a valid email address parsed as selectable text in the document body.
contact_email.fix: Include a standard selectable email address (e.g. name@domain.com) in the document body.

contact_phone.title: Phone Number Detection
contact_phone.description: Detects a standard telephone number in the document body.
contact_phone.fix: Add a standard telephone format in the contact section.

contact_links.title: Professional Links & URLs
contact_links.description: Checks for clickable or selectable URLs linking to GitHub, LinkedIn, or personal portfolio.
contact_links.fix: Include explicit text URLs for your GitHub and LinkedIn profiles.

date_format_consistency.title: Date Format Consistency
date_format_consistency.description: Checks whether dates follow a consistent convention (e.g., MMM YYYY or YYYY).
date_format_consistency.fix: Standardize all employment dates to a uniform format such as 'Jan 2023 - Present'.

roles_have_dates.title: Role Date Attribution
roles_have_dates.description: Ensures detected professional experience entries have associated start and end dates.
roles_have_dates.fix: Specify clear start and end dates next to every job title or project.

parse_breaks.title: Parse Boundary Breaks
parse_breaks.description: Detects dates accidentally concatenated directly into titles or companies without whitespace.
parse_breaks.fix: Separate dates and company/title strings with clear whitespace, pipes (|), or newlines.

action_verb_bullets.title: Action-Verb Bullet Openings
action_verb_bullets.description: Informational check: experience bullets starting with strong action verbs improve scannability.
action_verb_bullets.fix: Begin bullet points with active verbs like 'Architected', 'Built', 'Engineered', 'Optimized'.

paragraph_length.title: Dense Paragraph Check
paragraph_length.description: Flags dense text blocks exceeding 150 words without bullet points or paragraph breaks.
paragraph_length.fix: Break dense blocks of text into 2-3 concise bullet points.

keyword_stuffing.title: Repetitive Keyword Stuffing
keyword_stuffing.description: Flags repetitive identical keyword stuffing clusters that trigger spam filters.
keyword_stuffing.fix: Distribute skill mentions naturally in realistic project contexts instead of repeated keyword lists.

skill_spelling.title: Canonical Skill Nomenclature
skill_spelling.description: Flags non-standard spellings of common technologies where canonical naming is preferred.
skill_spelling.fix: Use canonical technology names (e.g. 'PostgreSQL' instead of informal abbreviations).
